proof_summary: A telescoping hypergeometric identity gives a base three-term recurrence, and multiplying its unnormalized $2\times2$ transfer matrices yields the recurrence for each arithmetic subsequence after explicit common factors are removed.  The remaining matrix-entry polynomial has alternating signs at consecutive negative half-integers, so degree counting locates all its roots in $(-m,0)$; reflection symmetry and suitable affine and even rescalings then produce $P,Q$ with the stated symmetry and root intervals (with $m=1$ handled by the explicit quadratic pair).
